question: Why is building therapeutic rapport so important before starting a psychosocial assessment?

options.A: It guarantees the client will take all prescribed medications on time.
options.B: It stops the client from ever feeling sad about their illness.
options.C: It helps the client feel safe enough to share honest personal feelings.
options.D: It allows the nurse to skip asking about family medical history.

explanation: Trust allows clients to lower their guard and discuss sensitive emotional and mental health topics openly with the nurse. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h3)

question: How does proper birth spacing protect a mother's health?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover nutrients and strength
options.B: It eliminates the need for any antenatal checkups
options.C: It completely prevents the onset of gestational diabetes
options.D: It guarantees that the next baby will be born full-term

explanation: Giving the body a break between pregnancies allows nutrient stores to refill, making future pregnancies much safer for mum. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: As a nurse, why is it important to look beyond obvious physical injuries when checking for abuse?

options.A: Because abusers always come along to every hospital visit
options.B: Because physical injuries always heal completely without leaving emotional scars
options.C: Because hospital rules do not allow us to write down emotional abuse
options.D: Because victims often come in with vague aches and pains instead of visible cuts or bruises

explanation: You've got this! Abuse shows up in many hidden ways. Patients might visit the clinic complaining of ongoing headaches, tiredness, or belly pain rather than obvious trauma. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why do many Nigerian patients choose private health facilities even though they must pay cash out of pocket?

options.A: They often perceive private care to have better quality and shorter waiting times
options.B: Private hospitals offer free medications to every registered citizen
options.C: Private clinics are entirely subsidized by federal government revenue
options.D: The law forbids them from visiting public hospitals for minor illnesses

explanation: Frustration with long queues and drug stockouts in public hospitals drives many citizens to private clinics, cost notwithstanding. It's a clear indicator of systemic challenges! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary reason lab techs treat every incoming patient sample as a biohazard?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory equipment stays warm during the night shift
options.B: To speed up the time it takes for bacteria to grow on agar plates
options.C: To prevent accidental infection of staff and the surrounding community
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing sterile glass slides

explanation: Safety first! Treating every sample like it's infectious ensures we always use proper barrier precautions to keep everyone safe. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h7)

question: Who should be involved when checking if an intersectoral health program was successful?

options.A: External foreign auditors exclusively
options.B: All participating sectors and community representatives
options.C: Private pharmaceutical company executives
options.D: Only the federal minister of health

explanation: Correct! Because many groups built the project together, everyone involved—including the community—needs a voice in evaluating how it went. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)

question: How does wanting a male child (son preference) affect family sizes in some communities?

options.A: It drives couples to keep trying for a boy, increasing total births

options.C: It automatically lowers the median age of marriage for women
options.D: It encourages families to stop childbearing after the first daughter

question: Where is the best place to hold a performance feedback meeting with a nurse?

options.A: The cafeteria during a crowded lunch hour
options.B: An open hallway near the patient care area
options.C: The busy nurses' station during shift change
options.D: A quiet, private room free from interruptions

explanation: Feedback is personal and sensitive. A quiet, private space helps both you and your manager talk freely without feeling rushed or exposed. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h5)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg normally take place in the female reproductive tract?

options.A: The interstitial segment
options.B: The isthmus
options.C: The ampulla
options.D: The fimbriae

question: Why might a patient feel a bit dizzy or have tummy discomfort shortly after taking their anti-parasite medication?

options.A: The medication causes immediate permanent damage to the liver cells
options.B: Parasites multiply rapidly inside the stomach in response to the drug
options.C: The drug destroys helpful gut bacteria needed for normal digestion
options.D: Mass destruction of parasites releases proteins that trigger mild reactions

explanation: You're doing great! When the medication kills off a lot of worms at once, their breakdown products can cause a brief allergic-type reaction in the body. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h6)

question: What is a great nursing action to help prevent constipation in a patient who just had surgery and is on bedrest?

options.A: Encouraging fluids and early walking as ordered
options.B: Applying hot water bottles directly to the lower belly
options.C: Giving a strong anti-diarrhea pill right away
options.D: Instructing the patient to stop eating all solid foods

explanation: Water softens the stool, and physical movement gets the bowels waking back up after surgery. Simple nursing care makes a massive difference! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h5)

question: What protective layer forms around the egg cell during early follicular development?

options.A: Zona pellucida
options.B: Antrum membrane
options.C: Tunica albuginea
options.D: Corpus luteum

explanation: Spot on! The zona pellucida acts like a special protective coat around the egg and later helps sperm bind to it during fertilization. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h3)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with heavy watery diarrhea and vomiting. What causes these intense symptoms?

options.A: Stomach acid production increases rapidly to destroy the liver
options.B: Infection causes complete destruction of the large intestine lining
options.C: A bacterial toxin forces massive water and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.D: Inflammation blocks all blood flow to the kidneys

explanation: The cholera germ releases a toxin that tricks the gut into dumping lots of water and salts, leading to heavy fluid loss. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T18#GNS313_U2_T18_h3)

question: How is prevalence different from incidence?

options.A: Prevalence counts both old and new cases together
options.B: Prevalence is calculated without using a denominator
options.C: Prevalence only measures diseases that last one day
options.D: Prevalence ignores people who are currently receiving care

explanation: Think of prevalence as the big picture: it adds up all existing cases, while incidence only counts the fresh, new ones! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of intravenous therapy over oral medication administration?

options.A: It prevents medications from being filtered by the kidneys.
options.B: It is completely painless and requires no technical skill.
options.C: It provides immediate systemic availability by bypassing the digestive tract.
options.D: It eliminates all potential risks of systemic infection.

explanation: Giving medications directly into a vein places them instantly into the bloodstream, avoiding the delay of digestion and liver processing. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why is severe anemia especially dangerous for a woman going into labor?

options.A: She has very little reserve to survive normal blood loss during delivery
options.B: She will automatically develop eclampsia within hours
options.C: Her contractions will completely stop during the first stage
options.D: Her baby will be born with severe bone deformities

explanation: You're doing great! Every delivery involves some blood loss. A mom with low blood levels (anemia) cannot afford even a small loss without sliding into shock. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h4)

question: During which early stage of HIV do patients often experience flu-like symptoms and a high viral load?

options.A: AIDS stage
options.B: Acute HIV infection
options.C: Remission phase
options.D: Clinical latency

explanation: Right after exposure, the acute stage hits with lots of virus replication and mild flu-like signs. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h4)

question: A nurse notices women in a village prefer risky home births due to tradition. What is the best first step?

options.A: Report all pregnant women in the village to the local police
options.B: Provide culturally sensitive education and build trust regarding hospital delivery benefits
options.C: Refuse to treat any woman who has previously given birth at home
options.D: Ignore the practice since culture cannot be influenced by health workers

explanation: Yarn true! Respecting people's culture while gently building trust is the best way to help them see the safety of hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why should a nurse always measure height and weight accurately instead of just guessing?

options.A: Inaccurate numbers can lead to dangerous errors in medication dosing
options.B: Patients get offended if the nurse guesses their size
options.C: Estimated numbers make the patient chart look untidy
options.D: Hospital management requires exact figures for billing purposes only

explanation: Many strong drugs, especially for children and critically ill patients, depend on exact body measurements so you don't accidentally give too much or too little. Great job learning the safety rules! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is the main strategy used to treat most cases of acute poisoning in the hospital?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic therapy
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation
options.C: Immediate surgical removal of the stomach
options.D: Supportive care and managing symptoms

explanation: Don't stress trying to memorize an antidote for everything—most poisons don't have one! The core treatment is simply keeping vital organs working smoothly until the body clears the poison on its own. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why is avoiding conflict usually an ineffective long-term strategy in nursing?

options.A: It always results in an immediate physical fight
options.B: It forces the nurse manager to fire the staff
options.C: Hospital management requires everyone to fight daily
options.D: The underlying problem usually remains unresolved and may worsen

explanation: Ignoring conflict sweeps issues under the rug, allowing tension to build up until a bigger crisis occurs. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is a core responsibility of a nurse in primary health care?

options.A: Setting national monetary policies for healthcare budgets
options.B: Conducting major surgical operations in tertiary hospitals
options.C: Assessing community needs and providing direct health education
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs in a laboratory setting

explanation: As a nurse, checking what your community lacks and teaching them how to stay healthy is a huge part of your primary care role. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h7)

question: What is the most important first step when a patient rings the bell asking for nausea medication?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water
options.B: Immediately administer a broad-spectrum 5-HT3 antagonist IV
options.C: Assess the character, frequency, and potential triggers of the nausea
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube to decompress the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Always assess first before giving meds. Understanding what's causing the nausea helps you pick the right treatment and catch hidden dangers. Excellent nursing judgment! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of holding a post-clinical nursing care conference?

options.A: To clean and sterilize all the equipment used during the practical session
options.B: To reflect on clinical experiences, share insights, and discuss patient care outcomes
options.C: To allow the hospital director to review student attendance registers
options.D: To punish students who arrived late to the hospital ward shift

explanation: Post-clinical conferences are your chance to decompress, talk about what you saw on the ward, ask questions, and learn from your peers' experiences. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h4)

question: Which hormone triggers the tiny muscle cells around the milk glands to squeeze during the let-down reflex?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is the hormone of love and contraction! It squeezes the myoepithelial cells around the alveoli so milk can flow down the ducts. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h6)

question: When someone breathes in gases or vapors, why do they get absorbed into the body so quickly?

options.A: Inhaled toxins always bypass the liver completely
options.B: The skin blocks all other forms of chemical entry
options.C: The stomach acid breaks down inhaled chemicals instantly
options.D: The lungs have a large surface area and a rich blood supply

explanation: Great clinical thinking! The tiny air sacs (alveoli) in our lungs offer a massive surface area packed with blood vessels. This lets inhaled substances pass straight into the bloodstream without wasting any time. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is one limitation of the placenta's protective barrier role against harmful substances?

options.A: It prevents the passage of essential hormones needed for growth
options.B: Many drugs and viral pathogens can still cross and harm the fetus
options.C: It destroys all maternal antibodies before they reach the fetus
options.D: It completely blocks all medications taken by the mother

explanation: While the placenta filters some toxins, it is not foolproof and allows many drugs, alcohol, and infections to pass through to the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h7)

question: What is a common socioeconomic barrier to good nutrition?

options.A: Inability to afford fresh, nutrient-dense food items
options.B: Excessive availability of free drinking water
options.C: A lack of personal interest in human anatomy
options.D: Too many cooking utensils in the household kitchen

explanation: Poverty and low income restrict access to quality food, often forcing reliance on cheap, calorie-dense foods with low nutritional value. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h7)

question: At what point in your clinical workflow should healthcare waste be sorted?

options.A: At the final incineration site
options.B: During the weekly municipal garbage collection
options.C: After transport to the central landfill
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right where you use it! Doing it immediately stops dangerous items from getting mixed up with regular trash. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: In nursing, what does the term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: Storing prescription pills in a secure kitchen cabinet
options.B: The use of multiple medications by a single patient
options.C: Taking only one tablet per day for high blood pressure
options.D: Buying drugs exclusively from a wholesale pharmacy

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking many drugs at once. It's super common in older adults, but it raises the risk of side effects and drug clashes. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the very first step of urine formation in the kidney?

options.A: Tubular secretion
options.B: Glomerular filtration
options.C: Peristaltic propulsion
options.D: Tubular reabsorption

explanation: Everything starts at the glomerulus! Blood pressure forces water and small particles out of the blood and into Bowman's capsule to kick off urine making. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h4)

question: A researcher wants to study how nurses feel about working night shifts by having open conversations. Which data collection method is best?

options.A: Numerical blood pressure screening
options.B: In-depth qualitative interviews
options.C: A rigid multiple-choice questionnaire
options.D: Laboratory biomarker blood testing

explanation: Open-ended interviews are fantastic because they let nurses express their true feelings in their own words. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why do many women hesitate to go back to a clinic for their next reproductive health checkup?

options.A: Nurses typically encourage too many follow-up visits
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable everywhere
options.C: They prefer managing all medical conditions independently at home
options.D: They experienced poor quality or disrespectful care previously

explanation: It's sad but true—if patients meet rude staff or lack privacy, they lose trust and stay away. Always aim to be the nurse who makes clients feel safe and welcome! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h1)

question: How long should you spend washing your hands with soap and water in a clinical setting?

options.A: 5 to 10 seconds
options.B: 3 to 5 minutes
options.C: 15 to 20 seconds
options.D: 40 to 60 seconds

explanation: Take your time! A proper clinical hand wash takes about 40 to 60 seconds—singing a quick song in your head helps pass the time. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is severe, sudden hypotension dangerous for a patient?

options.A: Sudden thickening of the heart muscle walls
options.B: Inadequate perfusion and oxygenation of vital organs
options.C: Immediate rupture of peripheral veins in the arms
options.D: Permanent blockage of the major coronary arteries

question: Why do many women with vulval tumours come to the hospital quite late?

options.A: Pain is usually so severe that patients refuse to leave home
options.B: Doctors routinely screen for vulval growths during annual exams
options.C: Symptoms are mistaken for common infections or cause embarrassment
options.D: The condition always spreads rapidly without any warning signs

explanation: You got it! Many patients delay coming in because they feel shy or mistake early signs for a simple skin irritation or infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which animal vector transmits the parasite that causes malaria?

options.B: Domestic housefly

question: Why should a nurse avoid raising the legs of a patient experiencing cardiogenic shock?

options.C: It can overload a failing heart with too much venous return
options.D: It prevents the administration of intravenous medications

question: Why must nurses rely on evidence-based practice when discussing complementary therapies with patients?

options.A: To ensure the chosen therapies are genuinely safe and effective
options.B: To force patients to stop using all traditional cultural customs
options.C: Because hospital management fines nurses who mention herbs

question: What is an essential post-procedure nursing check after an EPS?

options.A: Checking deep tendon reflexes in both upper arms
options.B: Removing all intravenous lines right before transport
options.C: Checking pulses and color in the extremity used for catheter insertion
options.D: Asking the patient to stand up and walk around immediately

question: How should a nurse handle cultural beliefs when teaching teenagers about reproductive health?

options.A: Delay all care until the client reaches the age of twenty-one
options.B: Balance cultural sensitivity with evidence-based health education and safety
options.C: Ignore community norms completely and lecture parents on backward customs
options.D: Refuse to provide any counseling to avoid angering community elders

explanation: You've got this! A great nurse respects community traditions while making sure young clients still get accurate, lifesaving health information. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h7)

question: If a patient has a shorter-than-normal fallopian tube, what are the two main ways this can happen?

options.A: Hormonal or mechanical
options.B: Congenital or acquired
options.C: Primary or secondary ischemic
options.D: Infectious or malignant

question: What is the primary goal of intra-natal care?

options.B: Ensuring the mother sleeps through delivery
options.C: Speeding up the duration of the first stage
options.D: Preventing the need for any pain relief

explanation: The main focus of intra-natal care is to safeguard the health and well-being of both the mother and the newborn throughout labor and birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h1)

question: Why should you place dentures back in a patient's mouth before family viewing, unless policy says otherwise?

options.A: It helps restore a natural facial appearance for the grieving family
options.B: Hospital regulations require all medical devices to remain intact
options.C: It prevents the jaw from locking shut during rigor mortis
options.D: It makes the body easier to transport to the mortuary van

explanation: Putting dentures in helps the patient look like themselves, which can bring a little bit of comfort to grieving family members. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge faced by local emergency responders in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant surplus of modern emergency helicopters in every local clinic
options.B: Poor inter-agency coordination during major crises
options.C: Delays in communication channels
options.D: Inadequate funding for disaster preparedness

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier when nursing vulnerable families?

options.A: Extreme poverty pushing health down the priority list
options.B: Cultural beliefs about what causes sickness
options.C: Having too much financial wealth and multiple luxury cars
options.D: Not having money for clinic transport

explanation: Spot on! Wealth is the opposite of vulnerability. Real barriers include poverty, transport costs, and conflicting cultural views. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h8)

question: What important advice should you give a patient who wants to start taking a daily multivitamin?

options.A: Taking five times the recommended dose will speed up healing

options.C: Supplements do not replace the benefits of eating a balanced, whole-food diet
options.D: There is no need to tell the doctor about over-the-counter vitamins

question: What does an 'in-kind' donation mean when talking about healthcare support?

options.A: Exchanging foreign currency at local black-market rates
options.B: Providing free land ownership titles to international aid workers
options.C: Supplying physical goods like medications and equipment instead of cash
options.D: Paying hospital staff salaries exclusively through electronic bank transfers

explanation: In-kind support simply means giving actual, tangible medical supplies and equipment rather than handing over raw cash. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why is the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) able to easily detect toxins in the blood?

options.C: It contains a high concentration of pain receptors
options.D: It lies outside the blood-brain barrier

question: Why do research proposals have to be checked by an ethics committee?

options.A: To ensure human rights and patient safety are fully protected
options.B: To calculate the exact profit the hospital will make
options.C: To decide which nursing journal will publish the final paper
options.D: To check if the grammar and spelling are completely perfect

explanation: Ethics boards are there to watch out for patients, ensuring that no study causes harm and that everything is done morally. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is continuous cardiac monitoring especially important for patients recovering from a heart attack?

options.A: It prevents them from moving around too much in bed
options.B: It automatically delivers shock therapy when needed
options.C: It helps catch dangerous rhythm changes early
options.D: It replaces the need for manual pulse checks completely

question: A patient with active tuberculosis usually reports which set of body-wide signs?

options.A: Sudden weight gain, severe headache, and lethargy
options.B: Night sweats, low-grade fevers, and weight loss
options.C: Constipation, blurred vision, and muscle spasms
options.D: High fever, severe joint swelling, and a skin rash

question: Why is community participation essential for the long-term success of public health interventions?

options.A: Traditional beliefs make outside nurses unwelcome without local approval
options.B: Local residents ensure facilities like water pumps are maintained after external aid projects end
options.C: Government health budgets are too small to pay local workers for maintenance
options.D: International donors refuse to send money unless villagers sign a legal contract

explanation: When communities take ownership, they maintain and protect health infrastructure long after initial external projects conclude. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h7)

question: In the early days of medicine, what kind of products caused the very first cases of serum sickness?

options.C: Animal-derived serum
options.D: Plant-based herbal teas

question: Why do nurses treat Wernicke encephalopathy as a true emergency?

options.C: It quickly spreads as a contagious infection

question: What is the main job of desmosomes in heart muscle cells?

options.C: Producing adenosine triphosphate for resting heart muscle

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like when it is most favorable for sperm survival around ovulation?

options.A: Yellow, foul-smelling, and clumpy
options.B: Thick, sticky, and dry like paste
options.C: Clear, stretchy, and slippery like egg white
options.D: Bloody and heavy like menstrual flow

question: What is the main difference between mechanical and biological vector transmission?

options.A: Biological vectors allow pathogens to develop inside their bodies, while mechanical vectors just carry them externally.

options.C: Mechanical vectors inject venom, while biological vectors only transmit viruses.
options.D: Mechanical vectors bite humans, while biological vectors only land on animal skin.

question: Which of these is considered a redundancy error in research writing?

options.C: Using the same font style for all headings in the paper
options.D: Placing explanatory footnotes below the table body

explanation: Listing every single table number word-for-word in your text is repetitive. Your text should just highlight the main trends instead! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h6)

question: What does the FIFO inventory method mean?

options.A: Financial-In, Financial-Out; tracks daily revenue collections
options.B: Fast-In, Fast-Out; speeds up the delivery of emergency medicines
options.C: Fixed-In, Fixed-Out; maintains rigid pricing for all drug types
options.D: First-In, First-Out; ensures older batches are used before they expire

explanation: Think 'First-In, First-Out'! The drugs that arrived first on the shelf should be given out to patients first, so nothing sits around long enough to expire. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h4)

question: What happens to a patient's taste buds after a few weeks of following a low salt diet?

options.A: They gradually adjust, making foods taste flavorful with less salt
options.B: They permanently lose the ability to taste warm foods
options.C: They demand twice as much salt to feel any satisfaction
options.D: They become completely numb to all sweet and bitter tastes

explanation: Taste buds adapt over time, meaning food that initially tastes bland will eventually become satisfying as the palate resets. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h7)

question: A community health nurse wants to lower malaria cases in a rural Nigerian village. Which action is the most practical primary health care step?

options.A: Stopping all routine vaccinations until malaria is completely eradicated
options.B: Admitting every healthy villager into the central hospital for observation
options.C: Waiting until an epidemic is declared before taking any action at all
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated bed nets and teaching mothers how to use them

explanation: Giving out bed nets and showing families how to use them directly protects people from nightly mosquito bites right in their homes. Excellent community nursing in action! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h7)

question: What marks the transition period of adolescence?

options.A: Fixed behavioral patterns
options.B: The cessation of brain development
options.C: Complete emotional and financial independence
options.D: Rapid physical, emotional, and social changes

explanation: Adolescence is defined as a transitional phase marked by rapid changes across physical, emotional, and social domains. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h1)

question: Who is widely recognized as the pioneer of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Mary Seacole
options.B: Linda Richards
options.C: Clara Barton
options.D: Florence Nightingale

explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing during the Crimean War by emphasizing sanitation, organization, and formal training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: A researcher decides to pick every 5th patient from the clinic register. Which sampling method is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Convenience sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: You nailed it! Going down a list at regular intervals (like every 5th or 10th person) is called systematic sampling. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which transmission route involves pathogens spreading via contaminated inanimate objects like door handles or instruments?

options.A: Airborne droplet transmission
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct contact transmission
options.D: Indirect contact transmission

explanation: Indirect contact occurs when a susceptible host touches a surface or object that harbors infectious agents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h3)

question: Which statistical test should you use to compare the average scores of two completely separate groups of patients?

options.A: Descriptive median
options.B: Independent t-test
options.C: Chi-square test
options.D: Paired t-test

explanation: Spot on! When your two groups are totally separate (like Ward A patients vs. Ward B patients), an independent t-test is your go-to tool. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which nursing action is most important for getting an accurate weight on a clinical scale?

options.A: Subtracting a standard clothing allowance from whatever scale value appears
options.B: Weighing the patient immediately after they have consumed a large meal
options.C: Ensuring the scale is calibrated and having the patient remove shoes and heavy coats
options.D: Using a spring-loaded bathroom scale brought from home for consistency

explanation: You got it! Checking that the scale is zeroed/calibrated and having the patient shed heavy outer garments ensures you are measuring the patient, not their jacket. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h5)

question: A community nurse is inspecting a pregnant woman's home delivery kit. Which item is UNNECESSARY or unsafe for newborn cord care?

options.A: A clean, sterile razor blade for cutting the cord
options.B: Traditional herbal mixture applied directly to the cut cord
options.C: Clean thread to tie off the umbilical cord securely
options.D: Soap and clean water for thorough handwashing

explanation: Applying unsterile substances like herbal mixtures to the umbilical cord introduces bacteria and causes severe neonatal infections like tetanus. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: What position should a patient be in during oral feeding to stop them from choking?

options.A: Slumped forward with the chin touching the chest
options.B: Lying flat on their back with one pillow
options.C: Reclining sideways on the left hip
options.D: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle

explanation: Correct! Sitting upright uses gravity to guide food safely down the food pipe instead of the windpipe. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h4)

question: A patient in her first trimester complains that her breasts feel heavy and sore. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: Early leakage of colostrum stretching the lactiferous ducts
options.B: Blockage of the lymphatic vessels inside the chest wall
options.C: Hormonal surges causing rapid tissue growth and increased blood flow
options.D: Infection of the milk ducts caused by elevated progesterone

explanation: That early tenderness is just the body's rapid way of gearing up! Hormones surge, blood flow increases, and the breast tissue starts growing rapidly. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h3)

question: At what age does a baby usually receive their first dose of the Pentavalent vaccine?

options.A: At 9 months of age
options.B: At birth
options.C: At 6 months of age
options.D: At 6 weeks of age

explanation: You nailed it! The routine immunization schedule starts the first Pentavalent dose at 6 weeks of age. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why do advanced tumors often become resistant to medical treatments like chemotherapy?

options.A: The body's immune system destroys the medication before it reaches the tumor
options.B: Chemotherapy drugs turn normal cells into malignant cancer cells
options.C: Genetic diversity creates varied cell populations with different drug resistance traits
options.D: Tumor cells develop a protective bone shell that blocks all medications

explanation: As mutations accumulate, cancer cells become diverse; while some cells die from treatment, resistant clones survive and multiply. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is checking skin elasticity (turgor) alone not a reliable way to check for dehydration in an older adult?

options.A: Older adults always refuse to let nurses pinch their hands or arms.
options.B: Aging skin naturally loses elasticity, making it look dehydrated even when it is normal.
options.C: Skin turgor only measures protein levels, not the body's water content.
options.D: Older adults produce too much natural sweat to measure skin fluid accurately.

explanation: Spot on! Older skin naturally loses its bounce, so it can look 'tented' even when the person is well-hydrated. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a community health program?

options.A: To punish staff members who failed to meet performance targets
options.B: To determine if the program met its goals and improved health outcomes
options.C: To increase the cost of healthcare services for local residents
options.D: To make sure no documentation paperwork is ever filed twice

explanation: Evaluation lets nurses see if their efforts actually helped the community or if changes are needed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h7)

question: Your patient weighs 154 pounds. What is their weight in kilograms?

options.A: 154 kg
options.B: 77 kg
options.C: 70 kg
options.D: 348 kg

explanation: Just divide pounds by 2.2! So, 154 ÷ 2.2 gives you 70 kg. Easy peasy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h4)

question: What do we call the action where food is pushed back inside the stomach to get mashed up even more?

options.A: Peristalsis
options.B: Retropulsion
options.C: Regurgitation
options.D: Segmentation

explanation: Think of retropulsion as the stomach's bounce-back action. Food gets pushed toward the closed exit valve and bounces back for another round of mixing! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does incidence differ from prevalence in community health data?

options.A: Incidence counts deaths, while prevalence counts active infections
options.B: Incidence is calculated yearly, while prevalence is calculated daily
options.C: Incidence measures new cases over time, while prevalence measures total existing cases
options.D: Incidence only applies to children, while prevalence applies to adults

explanation: Incidence tracks how fast a disease is spreading by counting new cases, whereas prevalence shows how widespread a condition currently is within the population. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended way to handle patient resistance?

options.A: Exploring the underlying emotional fears behind the refusal
options.B: Confronting the patient with strict authority and harsh demands
options.C: Using motivational interviewing to find common ground
options.D: Offering safe choices to give the patient back some control

explanation: Spot on! Coming down hard with bossy commands only makes a patient push back harder. Empathy and choices work way better than strict orders. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is nursing ethics so important when caring for patients at the end of life?

options.A: It ensures that hospitals never face lawsuits from grieving families
options.B: It gives nurses the legal authority to stop doctor's orders
options.C: It removes all emotional stress from the nursing profession
options.D: It helps nurses navigate complex moral choices and protect patient dignity

explanation: Ethical rules are like your compass. They help you balance high-tech hospital treatments with true human compassion, making sure vulnerable patients are treated right. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h1)

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between normal pregnancy breathlessness and a serious lung issue?

options.A: Serious lung problems disappear completely as soon as the patient drinks water
options.B: Normal dyspnoea lacks warning signs like chest pain, coughing blood, or low oxygen levels
options.C: Normal dyspnoea causes blue lips and severe finger clubbing
options.D: Normal dyspnoea only occurs when the patient is lying flat on her back

explanation: Ordinary shortness of breath feels safe and stable, but red flags like chest pain or low oxygen mean we must investigate right away. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h7)

question: What do we call infections that jump naturally between animals and humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infections
options.B: Autoimmune disorders
options.C: Zoonotic diseases
options.D: Chronic conditions

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections shared between animals and humans, like rabies or Lassa fever. Always good to keep this in mind for community health! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h3)

question: When is a nurse most likely to initiate intravenous therapy for a patient?

options.A: When the patient needs a rapid correction of severe dehydration.
options.B: When the patient is eating normally and taking daily multivitamin pills.
options.C: When topical skin cream is prescribed for a localized rash.
options.D: When a mild headache needs to be relieved over an eight-hour period.

explanation: Severe dehydration requires quick fluid volume restoration directly into the blood vessels, which can only be achieved effectively through IV therapy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h1)

question: The high-pressure alarm starts beeping loudly on the ventilator. As a nurse, what is a very common cause to check first?

options.A: An accidental extubation of the endotracheal tube
options.B: A deflation of the endotracheal tube cuff
options.C: A loose connection between the tubing and the patient
options.D: Secretions or mucus plug in the endotracheal tube

explanation: Think of it like a blocked straw—if mucus or a kink blocks the tube, the machine has to push harder to get air in, triggering that high-pressure alarm! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h4)

question: What is the name of the fluid-filled structure that implants into the lining of the womb?

options.A: Zygote
options.B: Blastocyst
options.C: Gamete
options.D: Morula

explanation: The blastocyst is the gorgeous little ball of cells ready to nestle comfortably into the uterine lining. You're doing brilliantly with these terms! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these actions is a serious breach of ethical nursing practice when taking a history?

options.A: Asking a family member to step out while taking a sensitive history
options.B: Discussing a patient's medical history in a public hospital hallway
options.C: Asking clarifying questions about the onset of a headache
options.D: Documenting the patient's social habits in their official chart

explanation: Well done! Talking about patient health details where others can hear breaks patient confidentiality and trust. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h8)

question: How should a nurse position a patient experiencing Superior Vena Cava Syndrome to help ease their symptoms?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillow
options.B: With their legs raised higher than their head
options.C: On their left side in the recovery position
options.D: Upright with the head elevated

explanation: Keeping the head of the bed elevated uses gravity to help reduce venous pressure and swelling in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of giving a patient a naloxone kit upon discharge for opioid use?

options.A: To cure the underlying brain changes caused by long-term addiction
options.B: To reverse a potential life-threatening opioid overdose
options.C: To prevent the daily cravings for heroin or prescription pills
options.D: To serve as a daily vitamin replacement during recovery

explanation: Naloxone is an opioid antagonist that rapidly blocks opioid receptors, restoring normal breathing during an accidental overdose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h6)

question: When is the ideal time to initiate discussions about goals of care and advance directives?

options.A: Only when family members begin arguing over medical bills
options.B: When the patient is unresponsive and unable to participate
options.C: Right after the patient is admitted to the intensive care unit
options.D: Before a medical crisis forces rapid, stressful decision-making

explanation: Early discussions prevent rushed decisions during emergencies and give patients ample time to reflect on their choices. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand water microbiology?

options.A: To help trace disease outbreaks and educate communities
options.B: To measure the exact depth of local rivers
options.C: To design large municipal water treatment plants
options.D: To chemically synthesize new antibiotics for hospitals

explanation: Nurses need this knowledge to connect water sources to community illnesses and teach safe hygiene habits. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h1)

question: A nurse manager assigns an unverified temporary nurse to a fragile patient without checking references, and the patient gets hurt. What legal issue pops up?

options.A: Automatic suspension of the hospital's corporate tax license
options.B: Vicarious liability shifting entirely away from the hospital entity
options.C: Negligent credentialing and direct administrative liability for the manager
options.D: Total exemption of the temporary nurse from personal legal penalties

explanation: Skipping background checks and putting unqualified people on the floor lands straight on the manager and the facility as negligent credentialing. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h6)

question: Which nursing action is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries and must be avoided?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands
options.B: Wearing clean gloves during procedures
options.C: Using single-dose medication vials
options.D: Performing hand hygiene before patient contact

explanation: Recapping used needles is a dangerous habit that frequently leads to accidental finger pricks. Keep safety first and drop them straight into the bin! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the main focus of geriatrics?

options.A: The social and economic policies affecting retirement
options.B: The medical care and treatment of older adults
options.C: The cellular biology of genetic mutations in youth
options.D: The psychological development of children and teens

explanation: Spot on! Geriatrics is simply the branch of healthcare that focuses on keeping older adults healthy and treating age-related conditions. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h1)

question: How long is the standard course of multi-drug therapy for a patient with multibacillary leprosy?

options.A: Exactly 6 months
options.B: 6 weeks
options.C: 3 to 5 years
options.D: 12 to 24 months

explanation: Multibacillary cases require a longer treatment duration, usually lasting 12 to 24 months, to clear the higher bacterial load. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why must nursing schools be accountable to the public and regulators?

options.A: To guarantee the university never runs out of money
options.B: To let students skip clinicals without penalty
options.C: So lecturers don't have to do performance reviews
options.D: To prove they train safe, competent nurses

explanation: Accountability builds public trust. It proves to patients and regulators that every graduate walking out of that school is safe to care for the public. [learn more](GST321_U9_T2#GST321_U9_T2_h6)

question: According to Nigerian client rights guidelines, what is a patient entitled to before undergoing a major procedure?

options.A: A written guarantee that recovery will take less than one week
options.B: Free transportation back to their home village after discharge
options.C: A clear explanation of the treatment and estimated costs
options.D: The personal phone number of the chief medical director

explanation: Clients have a right to transparent information regarding their care plan and financial obligations before treatment starts. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: If a pregnant mum temporarily eats less protein, what does the placenta do to protect the baby?

options.A: The placenta actively pumps amino acids to the fetus, maintaining its supply.
options.B: Amino acids turn into glucose inside the placenta.
options.C: The fetus stops growing entirely until the mother eats more meat.
options.D: Fetal amino acid levels drop immediately to match the mother's level.

explanation: Clever placenta! Even if mum's intake dips, active transport lets the placenta push extra amino acids over to keep the baby well-nourished. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h3)

question: How does uterine hyperstimulation lead to foetal hypoxia?

options.A: It shrinks the size of the umbilical cord vessels permanently
options.B: It prevents the placenta from refilling with oxygen between contractions
options.C: It forces the baby to breathe amniotic fluid too early
options.D: It causes the mother's blood pressure to rise dangerously high

explanation: If contractions are too close together without resting phases, blood flow through the uterine wall stops, starving the placenta of fresh oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h2)

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation nursing compared to acute care?

options.A: Providing permanent custodial long-term institutional care
options.B: Stabilizing immediate life-threatening medical crises
options.C: Curing the underlying pathological disease process
options.D: Restoring the patient to their highest level of independence

explanation: You've got this! While acute care is all about surviving the emergency, rehab is here to help patients get back on their feet and do as much for themselves as possible. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h1)

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a nurse working in community health?

options.A: It prevents patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.B: It allows the nurse to bypass standard medical protocols safely
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives financial awards from village chiefs
options.D: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build genuine trust

explanation: Spot on! Cultural humility means approaching people with an open, respectful mind, honoring their traditions while gently sharing health knowledge. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why does the CSSD follow a strict one-way workflow?

options.A: To make it easier for staff to walk around the department
options.B: To ensure sterilizers are close to the main entrance
options.C: To prevent clean items from crossing paths with dirty items
options.D: To reduce the electricity consumed by heavy machinery

explanation: A one-way flow makes sure that freshly cleaned and sterilized supplies never bump into or cross paths with dirty instruments. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: How can extreme poverty drive some families to practice early marriage?

options.A: By allowing the young bride to immediately secure high-paying employment
options.B: By guaranteeing free government housing for the newly wed couple
options.C: By reducing household financial burdens and sometimes yielding a bride price
options.D: By eliminating all taxes for families with married daughters

explanation: You got it! In severe economic hardship, some families feel pressured to marry off daughters to reduce mouths to feed or to gain financial help from a bride price. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T12#GNS312_U1_T12_h2)

question: What usually causes immune system problems?

options.A: Taking too many antibiotics
options.B: A single mutated gene passed down from parents
options.C: A mix of genetics, environment, and hormones
options.D: Sudden changes in body temperature

explanation: Most immune disorders don't happen from just one cause. Usually, a mix of internal factors (like your genes) and external things in your environment work together to trigger them. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h1)

question: A community nurse partners with local farmers and school headmasters to combat child malnutrition. Which concept does this action best demonstrate?

options.A: Private health insurance
options.B: Intersectoral linkages
options.C: Tertiary medical isolation
options.D: Acute hospital management

explanation: Partnering with agriculture and education sectors to address malnutrition is a classic example of intersectoral linkages. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: As a Nigerian nurse, what is a key part of your role when it comes to community nutrition?

options.A: Formulating industrial food additives in factories
options.B: Replacing all traditional farming with foreign grains
options.C: Educating communities and managing cases of malnutrition
options.D: Exporting local cash crops to international markets

explanation: That's right! Nurses are frontline educators. We spot nutritional gaps in our clinics and teach mothers the best ways to feed their families. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h6)

question: Which of these is a common everyday distraction during a home health visit?

options.A: Frequent interruptions from attending physicians
options.B: Mandatory shift-change meetings in the hallway
options.C: Strict hospital visiting hour regulations
options.D: Background noise from household sources and family members

explanation: Unlike quiet hospital wards, homes are full of life! TVs playing, pets barking, and family chatting can make focusing a bit tricky. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which side effect is very common after using a rescue inhaler like salbutamol?

options.A: Extreme sleepiness and slow breathing
options.B: Swelling of the feet and ankles
options.C: Fast heart rate and hand tremors
options.D: Severe yellowing of the skin and eyes

explanation: Rescue inhalers stimulate the sympathetic nervous system, which often leaves patients feeling a little jittery with a slightly fast heartbeat. It's totally normal and usually temporary! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h5)

question: What is the main job of dietary fats in infants and toddlers?

options.A: Acting as the main fuel source for red blood cells
options.B: Preventing childhood obesity and sluggishness
options.C: Supporting central nervous system development and brain growth
options.D: Supplying all the necessary vitamin C for the immune system

explanation: Exactly! Little ones need healthy fats because their growing brains and nerves depend heavily on them for proper development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h2)

question: You clear away some empty food cartons and clean paper towels from the nurses' station. Which bin should they go into?

options.A: Black or brown bin
options.B: Red cytotoxic container
options.C: Yellow bin with biohazard symbol
options.D: Yellow sharps safety box

explanation: Since paper towels and food wrappers are non-hazardous general waste, they belong in the ordinary black or brown bin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h7)

question: What makes a 'community of interest' different from a regular neighborhood community?

options.A: Being born in the same hospital maternity ward during the same year
options.B: Shared problems, professions, or health conditions rather than physical location
options.C: Living within the exact same fenced housing estate or neighborhood
options.D: Using the exact same public transport route to travel to work daily

explanation: A community of interest is built on shared bonds or struggles rather than geography. Think of a support group for mothers with sickle cell kids living in different parts of town! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which part of the cerebellar peduncle mainly sends outgoing motor correction signals away from the cerebellum?

options.A: Posterior cerebellar peduncle
options.B: Middle cerebellar peduncle
options.C: Superior cerebellar peduncle
options.D: Inferior cerebellar peduncle

explanation: The superior peduncle acts mainly as an exit route, sending output signals from the deep cerebellar areas up to higher brain centers like the thalamus. Great job reviewing your neuro pathways! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T22#GNS211_U3_T22_h1)

question: What is the easiest and most reliable way to track rapid fluid loss in a patient with diarrhoea?

options.A: Daily body weight measurements
options.B: Body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Changes in skin color on the face
options.D: Total number of hours slept per night

explanation: Weight drops fast when you lose body water. Hopping on the scale daily is one of the best ways to catch dangerous dehydration early. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why does the human body require a dual-circuit vascular system?

options.A: To ensure that blood flows in both directions simultaneously in arteries
options.B: To prevent high blood pressure from damaging delicate skin tissues
options.C: To allow the heart to rest while the lungs pump blood independently
options.D: To separate oxygenated blood from deoxygenated blood efficiently

explanation: Separating the pulmonary and systemic circuits ensures that oxygen-rich blood is kept distinct from oxygen-depleted blood for maximum delivery efficiency. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal when continuing education helps nurses drop old habits and adopt proven, modern methods?

options.A: Universal staffing
options.B: Preventing obsolescence
options.C: Mandatory licensing
options.D: Administrative control

explanation: Don't let the big word scare you—'preventing obsolescence' simply means making sure we don't use outdated or unsafe methods when science has found a better way! [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care?

options.A: To speed up the dying process
options.B: To replace hospital chemotherapy entirely
options.C: To improve quality of life and relieve suffering
options.D: To completely cure aggressive tumors

explanation: Palliative care is all about comfort, dignity, and making sure patients and their families feel supported when a cure isn't possible. Beautiful, compassionate nursing! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h8)

question: A pregnant patient reports severe chest pain spreading down her left arm. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report it immediately for cardiac evaluation
options.B: Suggest she take a strong antacid tablet right away
options.C: Reassure her that this is normal third-trimester heartburn
options.D: Advise her to lie down and drink cold milk

explanation: Chest pain spreading to the arm is a red flag for the heart! Never brush it off as simple heartburn. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h4)

question: What is the most common type of fainting experienced by otherwise healthy people?

options.A: Vasovagal syncope
options.B: Orthostatic hypotension
options.C: Neurological syncope
options.D: Cardiac syncope

explanation: Vasovagal syncope is triggered by everyday events like pain, stress, or standing too long and affects most people who faint. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why is trapping blood inside the penis (veno-occlusive mechanism) so important?

options.A: It closes off the urethral opening to prevent fluid loss during arousal
options.B: It pumps extra blood directly from the deep dorsal vein into the glans
options.C: It traps blood inside the corpora cavernosa to build high internal pressure
options.D: It releases large amounts of nitric oxide to keep the smooth muscle relaxed

question: Which medication is the go-to first choice for treating absence seizures in children?

question: What is the main nutritional catch of relying on just one single staple food, like only eating cassava for every meal?

options.A: It provides zero calories needed for daily physical activity
options.B: It lacks a complete profile of essential proteins and fats
options.C: It causes immediate and severe vitamin toxicity in adults
options.D: It contains too much dietary fiber for the human stomach

explanation: Spot on! While staples give great energy, eating only one thing leaves big gaps in other vital nutrients. Variety is always key! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T007#GNS227_U3_T007_h2)

question: Which lab tests do nurses commonly check to assess a patient's kidney function before giving medications?

options.A: Serum creatinine and BUN
options.B: ALT and AST liver enzymes
options.C: Red blood cell count and platelets
options.D: Sodium and potassium levels only

question: What does toxicology primarily study?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies in hospital patients
options.B: The manufacturing process of pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Microscopic organisms that cause infectious diseases
options.D: Poisons and their harmful effects on living things

explanation: Toxicology is specifically dedicated to understanding poisons, how they affect the body, and how to manage those effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which activity must a patient strictly avoid right after having nose or ear surgery?

options.B: Walking around the room
options.C: Drinking cool water
options.D: Forceful nose blowing

question: If a family suddenly loses income due to a job loss, what dietary change is most likely to happen first?

options.A: Stopping all food consumption completely for several days.
options.B: Switching entirely to imported gourmet food items.
options.C: Replacing expensive protein sources and fresh fruits with cheaper, starchy foods.
options.D: Growing all their own wheat and livestock in a small backyard.

explanation: Well done! When cash gets tight, families usually stretch their budget by swapping pricey proteins and fruits for filling, affordable starches. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h2)

question: When public health nurses talk about 'community structure', what are they mostly looking at?

options.A: The financial budget of the local government
options.B: How people are organized and how power is distributed
options.C: The physical blueprint of houses in a neighborhood
options.D: The exact number of hospital beds in a local clinic

explanation: Think of community structure as the backbone of the neighborhood: who holds influence, how groups connect, and how leadership works. Spotting this helps you know who to talk to when you want to start a health project! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the leading chronic health condition that results in lower limb amputation?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Diabetes mellitus

explanation: Diabetes damages blood vessels and nerves over time, making wounds hard to heal and often leading to tissue death. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why is post-natal care just as crucial as the care a mother gets during pregnancy?

options.A: Many serious health complications happen during the weeks after delivery.
options.B: The baby no longer needs any medical attention after birth.
options.C: Hormones return to normal instantly without any professional help.
options.D: It gives the mother time to rest away from her family members.

explanation: Spotting issues early saves lives! A large percentage of maternal and newborn complications happen right after birth, which is why close monitoring during the post-natal phase is a total lifesaver. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h1)

question: Why do midwives and nurses carefully check the maternal side of a delivered placenta?

options.A: To locate the insertion site of the amniotic membrane
options.B: To measure the exact length of the umbilical cord
options.C: To check for missing cotyledons that could cause bleeding
options.D: To confirm the baby's exact gestational age at birth

explanation: Those little lobes (cotyledons) must all be accounted for! If even a small piece stays behind in the uterus, it can cause severe postpartum hemorrhage. Always check your placenta! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h1)

question: How long must pain stick around before it is officially called chronic pain?

options.A: Less than 30 days
options.B: Longer than 3 to 6 months
options.C: More than 24 hours
options.D: Exactly one week

explanation: You're doing great! While acute pain heals quickly, chronic pain hangs around long past the normal healing time—usually defined as lasting over 3 to 6 months. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of emergency obstetric care networks?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal checkups
options.B: To reduce the overall birth rate in rural populations
options.C: To provide long-term family planning counseling
options.D: To treat sudden, life-threatening complications during birth

explanation: Correct! These networks ensure that when a sudden crisis hits during labor, mothers can get life-saving emergency care fast. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h6)

question: A patient having a severe asthma attack gets an intravenous steroid. What is the main goal of giving this in an emergency?

options.A: To thin out thick mucus plugs blocking the lower lung passages
options.B: To immediately relax tightened smooth muscle bands around the windpipe
options.C: To boost the patient's heart rate and increase oxygen delivery
options.D: To reduce swelling and inflammation inside the bronchial airways

explanation: Remember, steroids take a little time to change gene expression, so they aren't quick-fix muscle relaxers—they are used to bring down the dangerous swelling inside the airways. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h3)

question: When did the World Health Organization (WHO) publish its first Model List of Essential Medicines?
explanation: Great try! The WHO put out this very first list back in 1977 to bring order, safety, and priority to global drug markets. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: How can you make sure your patient truly understands a new reproductive medication?

options.C: By focusing only on how much the prescription costs
options.D: By explaining expected benefits, side effects, and warning signs clearly

question: Why must a nurse instruct a patient to remove all metal jewelry and hairpins before a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: The scanner's suction will pull metal objects into the machine.
options.B: Metal interacts with the magnetic field to cause severe burns.
options.C: Metal objects cause artifacts that ruin the clarity of the images.
options.D: Metal pieces block the patient from breathing properly.

question: What is the medical term for an infection of the lower urinary tract involving the bladder?

options.A: Glomerulonephritis
options.B: Urethral stricture
options.C: Pyelonephritis
options.D: Cystitis

question: Which type of parasitic egg is known for having a little lid (operculum) or a sharp spine?

question: Which condition is a clear contraindication for routine nasotracheal suctioning?

options.A: Severe bleeding disorders or severe nasal trauma

options.C: A mild low-grade fever without respiratory changes
options.D: Being sleepy but easily waking up when spoken to

question: How does a memory lapse differ from a mistake in everyday nursing practice?

options.A: A lapse is a memory failure, whereas a mistake is a planning failure
options.B: A lapse happens during surgery, whereas a mistake happens in the ward
options.C: A lapse involves equipment, whereas a mistake involves medication
options.D: A lapse is intentional, whereas a mistake is always accidental

explanation: Think of it this way: a lapse is forgetting a step because you got distracted, while a mistake is following a faulty plan because of incomplete knowledge. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h2)

question: How do the kidneys respond when the blood becomes too acidic?

options.A: By retaining hydrogen ions and excreting bicarbonate

options.C: By slowing down the filtration rate of the glomerulus

question: Why is regular walking encouraged for patients with stable peripheral artery disease?

options.A: It forces venous blood upward by squeezing calf muscles
options.B: It helps tiny new blood vessels (collateral vessels) grow around blockages
options.C: It melts away calcified plaque in the leg arteries
options.D: It lowers heart rate and stops vasospasms

question: Which type of medication is usually the first choice for treating post-abortion cramps?

question: Which hormones are mainly responsible for breaking down fat and muscle during the stress of surgery?

question: When a patient has vulval varicosities, which other body part should you check as a nurse?

question: What is the primary purpose of secondary neurological prevention?

options.A: Catching disease early and halting its progress
options.B: Performing major neurosurgery in emergency rooms
options.C: Preventing people from ever starting to smoke
options.D: Teaching chronic patients how to use a wheelchair

question: Why should you see bath time as a special clinical opportunity rather than just a boring chore?

question: Which design offers the highest level of evidence by using all three core elements?

question: What is the primary physical change that happens first in a joint affected by osteoarthritis?

question: Why is it super important for bedside nurses to have a voice when testing new hospital software?

question: You just received a new supply of liquid pentavalent vaccines for your clinic fridge. Where should you place them?

question: When is it appropriate to begin the secondary survey on an emergency patient?

question: Why do hospitals nowadays rarely give whole blood to patients?

question: Why is knowing the chain of infection so helpful for nurses?

question: A mother denies her toddler eggs due to a local belief. What is the biggest danger of this practice?

question: Which of these is a classic sign of a torn urethra in a male patient?

question: What is the most common reason people develop Wernicke encephalopathy?

question: What makes an intraarterial line different from a standard intravenous (IV) line?

question: What is the main point of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

question: A clinic nurse reads about a brilliant new wound care gadget, but her clinic lacks the budget and steady electricity to run it. What should she consider?

question: Which IV fluid is the only safe choice to use for priming blood tubing?

question: Why must nurses strongly advise patients NEVER to squeeze or pop a vulval cyst at home?

question: What simple trick involves writing off-topic discussion points on a separate board to address later?

question: What does the basal metabolic rate measure?

question: Three hours after knee surgery, a patient complains that their toes feel cold and numb. What is your very first action?

question: What is one of the best ways a nurse can comfort parents facing an unexpected preterm birth?

question: What causes the area around an infected wound to swell up?

options.D: A buildup of dead red blood cells

question: What is the biggest perk of using a mixed methods design in nursing research?

options.A: It shortens the data collection phase to a single day
options.B: It provides a more complete picture by balancing numbers with human experience
options.C: It eliminates the need for any statistical calculations

explanation: Numbers tell us the 'how much,' but stories tell us the 'why.' Combining both gives us a much richer, more human understanding of healthcare challenges. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main goal of having a 'unified command' during a local emergency?

question: Which type of vitamin is most likely to cause toxicity if taken in excess because they store up in body fat?

question: Why is a waste factor or buffer stock added when calculating injection commodities?

question: Which type of small intestinal disorder involves long-term, deep inflammation of the bowel wall that can form strictures and fistulae?

question: Your patient suddenly complains of lower back pain and chills mid-transfusion. What is your immediate nursing action?

question: What chemical signal do growing tumors release to tell new blood vessels to grow?

question: What imaging test is considered the absolute gold standard for spotting a pituitary tumor?

question: Why do strict, one-size-fits-all meal plans usually fail in real life?

options.C: They ignore personal preferences and financial realities

question: How do early childhood attachment disruptions affect a person later in life?

question: What should a home health nurse do when preparing to change a sterile wound dressing in a cluttered living room?

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to handle confounding when designing a study?
