options.B: Intentionally falsifying data to match the hypothesis
options.C: Randomizing participants if possible
options.D: Restricting the study to specific age groups

explanation: Never fake data! Falsifying results is serious scientific misconduct. We control confounders through smart study design instead. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h5)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a visual disability?

options.A: Any mild eye infection treated with antibiotic drops
options.B: Total loss of hearing alongside failing sight
options.C: Temporary blurriness caused by eye strain
options.D: Permanent vision loss not corrected by standard glasses

explanation: Visual disability specifically refers to lasting impairment that remains even after standard medical or optical corrections like eyeglasses are applied. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which of these is a great example of the teach-back method in action?

options.A: Is there anything confusing about taking two tablets every morning?
options.B: Do you understand all the instructions I gave you about your heart medication?
options.C: Can you read this pamphlet out loud to prove your vision is fine?
options.D: Show me how you plan to use your blood glucose meter before you leave today.

explanation: Asking 'show me' or 'tell me in your own words' beats a simple 'do you understand?' every single time. Brilliant clinical communication! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why might the standard 0-to-10 numeric pain scale be tricky to use for an adult with severe dementia?

options.A: Numeric scales only work for surgical wounds
options.B: Patients with dementia lose the ability to speak at all
options.C: They will always just say ten no matter what
options.D: They may struggle to connect a number to how they feel

explanation: Well reasoned! Numbers are abstract concepts. For patients with cognitive changes, we often need to rely on facial expression charts or physical behavior cues instead. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h4)

question: What happens to a woman's cervical mucus during her fertile window to help conception?

options.A: It becomes clear, stretchy, and slippery
options.B: It develops a foul odor and heavy discharge
options.C: It dries up completely to block germs
options.D: It turns thick, sticky, and brownish

explanation: High estrogen turns cervical mucus into a friendly, slippery highway that helps swimming sperm travel easily toward the egg. Nature is amazing! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling vaccines?

options.A: To make the injection feel more comfortable for the patient
options.B: To prevent the growth of harmful bacteria inside the glass vial
options.C: To ensure the chemical potency and effectiveness of the vaccine
options.D: To extend the manufacturer expiration date by several years

explanation: Brilliant! Heat can easily ruin the active ingredients in vaccines, rendering them useless if the cold chain breaks. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h5)

question: A surgical drain was flowing nicely, but now it has suddenly stopped. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The body has miraculously stopped producing all normal inflammatory fluid
options.B: The collection container is now completely sterile and safe to remove
options.C: The surgical wound has finished healing completely on its own
options.D: The tube might be blocked or kinked inside or outside the patient

explanation: When output stops abruptly, don't assume a miracle healing! Always check the tubing first for a clot, mucus, or a pesky kink. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h4)

question: How do patients with illness anxiety disorder usually react to normal, everyday body sensations like a slight muscle twitch?

options.A: They report them exclusively to family members only
options.B: They ignore them completely as routine physiology
options.C: They misinterpret them as signs of catastrophic disease
options.D: They use them to plan healthy physical exercise routines

explanation: Think of it this way: a normal minor ache gets blown completely out of proportion, making the patient convinced it's a hidden, dangerous sickness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h1)

question: What usually happens if a clinic or hospital runs without clear objectives?

options.A: Operational costs drop significantly across all departments.
options.B: Staff morale improves because there is less pressure.
options.C: Patient satisfaction automatically reaches maximum levels.
options.D: Resources are wasted and priorities become unclear.

explanation: Without a clear roadmap, everyone ends up pulling in different directions, leading to wasted time and resources. Clear goals keep the team aligned! [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why do we write nursing research reports?

options.A: To share study findings so others can improve patient care
options.B: To prove that the researcher is an expert statistician
options.C: To fulfill a mandatory graduation requirement for students
options.D: To criticize current hospital management and policies

explanation: The main goal of nursing research is to find better ways to care for patients and share those discoveries with the healthcare team! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h1)

question: Why is stepping on the scale to check daily body weight so crucial in the care plan for kidney failure?

options.A: It measures how well the bone marrow is producing red blood cells.
options.B: It helps calculate the exact amount of protein the patient needs to eat.
options.C: It is the most sensitive daily indicator of fluid retention or loss.
options.D: It indicates whether the patient is taking their iron supplements on time.

explanation: Numbers don't lie! A sudden weight gain over a day or two almost always means the kidneys are struggling and the body is holding onto dangerous amounts of fluid. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h7)

question: Who holds overall administrative and clinical responsibility for running a hospital ward?

options.A: The senior ward orderly
options.B: The Chief Medical Director
options.C: The hospital head pharmacist
options.D: The Ward Manager or Nursing Officer in Charge

explanation: The Ward Manager handles staff scheduling, clinical standards, and general administrative duties on the unit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main goal when giving culturally sensitive nutrition counseling?

options.A: To eliminate all traditional cooking methods from the community
options.B: To adapt healthy eating advice to fit the patient's local lifestyle and foods
options.C: To replace all local food items with expensive imported supplements
options.D: To force every patient to adopt a westernized diet style

explanation: Good nursing care works with what the patient already eats and enjoys, making healthy lifestyle changes realistic and sustainable. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a subacute care facility?

options.A: Treating minor outpatient ailments and routine infections
options.B: Managing acute life-threatening surgical emergencies
options.C: Providing short-term rehabilitation and medical management
options.D: Offering permanent residential care for healthy elders

explanation: Spot on! Subacute care bridges the gap between the busy hospital ward and home, giving patients targeted rehab and recovery support. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h1)

question: When doing nursing research, what are the three main levels used to group literature sources?

options.A: Primary, secondary, and tertiary sources
options.B: Published, unpublished, and grey sources
options.C: Clinical, historical, and theoretical sources
options.D: Qualitative, quantitative, and mixed sources

explanation: You've got this! We group literature into three tiers based on how close the information is to the original study. Primary, secondary, and tertiary keep our research organized. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h1)

question: A patient with severe kidney failure is prescribed a magnesium-based laxative. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Consult the doctor because magnesium can accumulate dangerously in renal failure
options.B: Switch the medication to a bulk-forming agent without telling the physician
options.C: Advise the patient to take the drug with twice as much table salt
options.D: Administer the medication immediately as ordered without any extra precautions

explanation: Brilliant! Kidneys filter out magnesium; if they aren't working well, the mineral builds up to dangerous levels. Always check with the prescriber. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h4)

question: When should you seal and replace a sharps disposal box?

options.A: When it is completely filled to the absolute brim
options.B: Whenever the outer cardboard gets slightly dusty
options.C: When it is three-quarters full
options.D: At the end of every single calendar month

explanation: Stop at the three-quarter mark! Waiting until it's overflowing invites accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why do vulnerable population groups need special healthcare approaches instead of regular programs?

options.A: Government policy forbids them from visiting general clinics
options.B: They refuse to take any standard orthodox medications
options.C: They face unique barriers like poverty, isolation, and stigma
options.D: Standard programs are too expensive for hospitals to run

explanation: Spot on! Because of hurdles like distance, poverty, or discrimination, standard health programs often fail to reach them without special adjustments. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h2)

question: What are the three core things the TNM staging system looks at?

options.A: Temperature, Nutrition level, and Medication history
options.B: Time of onset, Number of lumps, and Medical history
options.C: Total blood count, Nerve damage, and Muscle tone
options.D: Tumor size, Node involvement, and Metastasis

explanation: T = Tumor size, N = Node spread, M = Metastasis (spread to distant organs). You'll use this staging system all through clinicals! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT something a bedside nurse is supposed to do during diagnostic tests?

options.A: Performing the official radiological interpretation of the scan
options.B: Monitoring the patient's vital signs throughout the procedure
options.C: Checking the insertion site for bleeding afterward
options.D: Verifying that informed consent has been obtained

explanation: Reading and officially interpreting scans is the job of trained radiologists or doctors, though nurses definitely watch for patient safety! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why does a malnourished patient usually take longer to recover from an infection?

options.A: Malnourished patients always refuse their oral medications
options.B: Hospital insurance policies automatically extend stays for underweight individuals
options.C: Their body lacks the nutritional fuel needed to fight infection and heal
options.D: Doctors cannot discharge anyone who has lost any body weight

explanation: You've got this! Healing requires energy and raw materials. Without them, recovery slows down and complications take longer to clear up. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h4)

question: What structural feature keeps the trachea open and stops it from collapsing?

options.A: Smooth muscle sheets inside the lumen
options.B: Horseshoe-shaped cartilage rings
options.C: Dense networks of elastic ligaments
options.D: Thick layers of stratified epithelium

explanation: Think of those horseshoe-shaped cartilage rings as sturdy scaffolding that keeps the windpipe open against everyday neck pressures. Simple and brilliant! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is communication considered a two-way process in the IEC framework?

options.A: It focuses only on passing medical news from the hospital to the village
options.B: It requires two different nurses to speak at the same community meeting
options.C: It means printing health materials in both English and a local language
options.D: It involves listening to community feedback and addressing local fears

explanation: Effective communication in IEC goes beyond just giving orders; it requires listening to what the community has to say and clearing up doubts. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle does the nursing team actually carry out the test and record initial observations?

options.A: Plan
options.B: Study
options.C: Act
options.D: Do

explanation: Awesome! The 'Do' phase is when you roll up your sleeves, try out the idea on a small scale, and write down what happens. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h6)

question: You need to add more water to a running steam generator. What is your very first step?

options.A: Ask the parent to hold the steam nozzle away
options.B: Pour cold water slowly while the unit is still boiling
options.C: Turn off and unplug the unit before adding water
options.D: Cover the hot metal parts with a dry towel first

explanation: Always power down and unplug first! This protects you from electrical shocks and nasty steam burns. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which simple device is used to check how fast a patient can forcefully blow air out of their lungs?

options.A: Sphygmomanometer
options.B: Peak flow meter
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Pulse oximeter

explanation: Spot on! A peak flow meter is a handy little tool nurses use to keep an eye on airflow in asthma patients. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h6)

question: Which activity is generally not safe for someone with unmanaged seizures?

options.A: Swimming alone in deep water
options.B: Reading books in a well-lit room
options.C: Walking outside during the daytime
options.D: Drinking plenty of clean water

explanation: Safety first! If a seizure hits while swimming alone, the risk of drowning is extremely high. Advising against solo swimming is a crucial part of patient education. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h9)

question: Why might a clinical protocol that works wonderfully in an adult surgical ward fail if copied directly into a children's ward?

options.A: Adult patients always recover faster than pediatric patients regardless of care
options.B: Surgical nurses have much higher educational degrees than pediatric nurses
options.C: Children's wards never use standard hospital protocols of any kind
options.D: Different units have unique patient needs, workflows, and environmental contexts

explanation: Every ward has its own unique vibe and patient needs! We always need to tweak a practice to fit the receiving unit rather than copy-pasting blindly. [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is one of the best things a community health nurse can do to fight gender bias?

options.A: Forcing patients to abandon their cultural beliefs
options.B: Reporting every community member to the police
options.C: Limiting health education to male household heads
options.D: Providing respectful, judgment-free care to all patients

explanation: Creating a safe, welcoming clinic space where everyone feels respected is a powerful nursing action against discrimination. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h8)

question: What is the main benefit of storing energy as fats (lipids) instead of carbohydrates?

options.A: Fats provide more than double the energy per gram
options.B: Fats do not require oxygen for complete breakdown
options.C: Lipids dissolve easily in water for rapid transport
options.D: Lipids can be converted directly into red blood cells

explanation: Fats are super energy-dense! They pack more than twice the energy punch per gram compared to carbs, making them a very compact way to store backup fuel. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why are nurses strongly advised NOT to recap used needles?

options.A: It violates hospital rules regarding plastic waste recycling
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of accidental needle stick injuries
options.C: It damages the sharp tip making it useless for the next patient
options.D: It wastes valuable nursing time during busy medication rounds

explanation: Trying to guide a tiny cap back onto a used needle is one of the quickest ways to accidentally poke yourself. Drop it straight into the safety box instead! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h7)

question: A nurse assesses an adult patient with suspected acute osteomyelitis. Which set of findings is most expected?

options.A: Yellowing of the eyes, dark urine, and severe abdominal cramping
options.B: High fever, localized bone pain, swelling, and extreme tenderness
options.C: Numbness in both hands, low blood pressure, and a dry cough
options.D: Painless joint stiffness, dry skin, and generalized hair loss

explanation: Acute osteomyelitis classically triggers both systemic signs of infection like fever and distinct local signs like pain, warmth, and swelling at the bone site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the main reason we roll a laboring patient onto her side during an emergency?

options.A: To prepare the patient's back for an epidural anesthetic injection
options.B: To relieve pressure on the vena cava and improve blood flow to the fetus
options.C: To completely stop the progression of active labor contractions
options.D: To make it easier to perform a sterile vaginal examination

explanation: Lying flat lets the heavy uterus press on major blood vessels. Turning her to the side opens up blood flow and sends vital oxygen straight to the baby! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h7)

question: Why is a functional assessment necessary when caring for someone with a physical disability?

options.A: To prove that the patient is unable to walk
options.B: To diagnose the original cause of the injury
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital equipment
options.D: To match nursing interventions with the patient's actual capabilities

explanation: Assessing what a patient can still do prevents nurses from doing tasks the patient is fully capable of managing themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who insists on getting an injection instead of pills for a mild illness?

options.A: Explain that oral medications are often just as effective and much safer
options.B: Tell the patient that injections are illegal for treating mild illnesses
options.C: Refuse to speak with the patient until they accept the prescribed pills
options.D: Administer a harmless saline injection to satisfy their psychological need

explanation: Patient education works best when it's kind and respectful. Clear up the myth about injections while highlighting why safe oral meds are great. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h9)

question: What is the main purpose of an under-water seal drainage system?

options.A: To restore negative pressure in the pleural space
options.B: To measure the exact daily urine output of a patient
options.C: To pump sterile water directly into the lung tissue
options.D: To deliver high-flow oxygen straight into the chest cavity

explanation: The primary goal of chest tube drainage is to evacuate air or fluid, thereby re-establishing the normal negative pressure needed for lung expansion. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the main goal of providing nutrition care for patients in the hospital?

options.A: Preventing malnutrition and supporting healing
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital food services
options.C: Replacing the need for doctor-ordered diets
options.D: Ensuring patients gain weight during every stay

explanation: Great job! Good nutrition keeps the body strong so it can fight off infections and heal wounds faster. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h1)

question: Which of these statements about injectable contraceptives is FALSE?

options.A: They prevent pregnancy by stopping ovulation
options.B: They require regular repeat doses to remain effective
options.C: They lead to permanent sterility after one dose
options.D: They can cause changes in monthly bleeding patterns

explanation: Injectables do not cause permanent infertility! Once you stop, fertility naturally returns after the drug clears the system. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h5)

question: Which teaching style works best when you are educating a patient who was just diagnosed with diabetes?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on severe complications like kidney failure
options.B: Tailoring information to fit the patient's daily routine and lifestyle
options.C: Insisting that they completely change their diet in one single day
options.D: Handing them a complex medical textbook to read overnight

explanation: Teaching works best when it's practical, personalized, and fits smoothly into the patient's real everyday life. Fantastic work finishing this set! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h8)

question: A community clinic wants to stop teenagers from dropping out of care. What should they do first?

options.A: Require formal written permission from local chiefs
options.B: Move the clinic to a remote location outside the city
options.C: Offer drop-in services and reduce long waiting times
options.D: Increase fees to cover new facility decorations

explanation: Spot on! Cutting down long delays and allowing flexible drop-in visits keeps young people engaged and willing to return. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h4)

question: A patient on a ventilator has low oxygen and is straining their neck muscles just to breathe. What's the best nursing diagnosis here?

options.A: Impaired Social Interaction
options.B: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.C: Risk for Constipation
options.D: Ineffective Breathing Pattern

explanation: Spot on! When you see a patient working way too hard with their accessory muscles and struggling for oxygen, their breathing pattern is definitely ineffective and needs your help. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is community health nursing so important to primary health care in Nigeria?

options.A: It manages all tertiary hospital admissions across the country
options.B: It brings preventative and basic health services directly to local populations
options.C: It exclusively handles complex surgical procedures in rural areas
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors in government hospitals

explanation: You got it! By stepping into local clinics, schools, and homes, community health nurses make sure everyday preventative care actually reaches where people live. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why does severe dehydration eventually cause organs to stop working in a child?

options.A: Electrolyte imbalances cause immediate paralysis of the heart
options.B: The kidneys stop working because they are overworked by toxins
options.C: Reduced blood volume leads to poor oxygen delivery to tissues
options.D: The digestive tract bursts from lack of internal pressure

explanation: Think of blood like a delivery truck carrying oxygen. When water is lost, total blood volume drops, meaning vital organs don't get the oxygen they need to keep running smoothly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h1)

question: Calcium, potassium, and iron belong to which group of nutrients?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Vitamins
options.C: Minerals
options.D: Proteins

explanation: These are essential minerals! They help build strong bones, balance your body fluids, and carry oxygen in your blood. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h3)

question: Which action best supports the emotional needs of a patient newly diagnosed with a blood disorder?

options.A: Leaving educational brochures on the bedside table and leaving
options.B: Providing active listening and validating their concerns
options.C: Directing all emotional questions strictly to the attending physician
options.D: Telling them not to worry because things could be worse

explanation: A new diagnosis is scary. Listening with empathy and validating their feelings builds trust and helps them cope better. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h7)

question: Why is amenorrhoea best thought of as a warning sign rather than a disease on its own?

options.A: It always resolves on its own without any medical treatment
options.B: It cannot be measured with standard laboratory blood tests
options.C: It only happens during normal life stages like pregnancy
options.D: It is a symptom caused by an underlying physical or hormonal problem

explanation: Just like a fever, amenorrhoea is your body's way of telling you that something else is throwing off its normal hormone balance. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h1)

question: A patient with severe amoebiasis suddenly gets a rigid, board-like tummy and severe pain all over. What is your primary worry as a nurse?

options.A: Normal recovery after medication
options.B: Temporary gas accumulation
options.C: Bowel perforation and peritonitis
options.D: A mild medication side effect

explanation: Spot on! A rigid abdomen is a classic red flag for peritonitis caused by a perforated bowel. Quick action is life-saving! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is likely to happen if a hospital sets its DRF mark-up to zero percent?

options.A: The pharmacy will gradually lose purchasing power due to inflation and waste, leading to stock-outs
options.B: Patients will buy more drugs because they are cheaper, making the fund richer
options.C: The hospital will save money on administrative costs and paperwork
options.D: The government will send extra money every month to maintain the exact same inventory level

explanation: Without a small mark-up to cover waste and inflation, your capital gradually shrinks until you can no longer afford to restock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the puborectalis muscle in bowel control?

options.A: Pumps blood away from the hemorrhoidal veins
options.B: Produces mucus to lubricate the anal canal
options.C: Senses the chemical composition of the stool
options.D: Creates an angle that helps keep stool in the rectum

explanation: The puborectalis muscle pulls the rectum forward to form a sharp bend, which acts as a mechanical barrier against accidental leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do some sleeping pills sometimes fail to give patients truly refreshing rest?

options.A: They permanently damage the brainstem respiratory control centers
options.B: They cause severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance during sleep
options.C: They distort normal sleep stages by suppressing deep and rapid eye movement sleep
options.D: They cause the patient to sleep for less than two hours per night

explanation: Certain sleeping pills mess with your natural sleep cycle, blocking you from getting enough of that crucial deep sleep and REM rest. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h2)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy do the baby's main body organs actively form?

options.A: Weeks 10 to 14
options.B: Weeks 32 to 36
options.C: Weeks 3 to 8
options.D: Weeks 20 to 24

explanation: Brilliant! Weeks 3 to 8 are known as the embryonic period, when all the primary organ systems are shaped and laid down. Keep up the great momentum! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h2)

question: What is the truest way to know if a continuing education training program was actually successful?

options.A: Checking how many participants filled out the seminar evaluation form
options.B: Verifying that all attendees stayed awake throughout the presentation
options.C: Observing if nurses apply what they learned to improve patient bedside care
options.D: Counting how many hours the lecture room lights remained switched on

explanation: Paper evaluations are nice, but real success shows up at the bedside when patients receive better, safer care because of what you learned! [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h5)

question: How does widespread tobacco use create a double challenge for Nigeria's health system?

options.A: It reduces the overall population so much that clinics have no patients to treat
options.B: It causes nurses to leave public clinics for international job opportunities
options.C: It forces hospitals to buy expensive imported equipment for infectious diseases only
options.D: It requires managing rising lifestyle diseases alongside existing infectious disease challenges

explanation: Clinics have to juggle treating traditional infectious diseases while also handling a growing wave of chronic illnesses caused by tobacco. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h2)

question: What special room feature do you need for a patient on Airborne Precautions?

options.A: Negative pressure airflow
options.B: An attached private sunroom
options.C: Open windows for natural breeze
options.D: Positive pressure ventilation

explanation: A negative pressure room pulls air in instead of blowing it out into the hallway when the door opens, trapping germs inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which body receptor is mainly responsible for the pain-relieving power of strong opioids?

options.A: Alpha receptor
options.B: Mu receptor
options.C: Beta receptor
options.D: Gamma receptor

explanation: The mu receptor is the main target for opioids to kill pain, though it's also why strong opioids can cause drowsiness and slow breathing. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h4)

question: A patient expresses deep shame and refuses visitors due to faecal incontinence. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Provide empathetic listening and discuss discreet coping strategies
options.B: Encourage the patient to ignore the problem completely
options.C: Restrict all family members from visiting permanently
options.D: Tell the patient that everyone experiences this eventually

explanation: Validating the patient's feelings and offering practical solutions helps restore dignity and reduces anxiety related to the condition. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h8)

question: What type of tissue mainly makes up the deeper part of the dermis (the reticular layer)?

options.A: Dense irregular connective tissue
options.B: Simple squamous epithelium
options.C: Loose areolar connective tissue
options.D: Hyaline cartilage tissue

explanation: You nailed it! This tough tissue is packed with collagen fibers that give your skin strength and help it resist tearing when stretched. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why do we always push iron and folate supplements during antenatal care?

options.A: To cure existing chronic infections in the uterus
options.B: To increase the total body weight of the mother
options.C: To speed up the physical growth of the mother's hair
options.D: To prevent anemia and neural tube defects in the baby

explanation: Iron keeps the mother's blood strong and fights off tiredness (anemia), while folate protects the baby's developing brain and spine. It's a powerful combo! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h2)

question: Why is verifying a patient's identity critical during a tele-nursing consultation?

options.A: To ensure the patient is using an approved brand of mobile phone
options.B: To prevent unauthorized persons from receiving confidential health information
options.C: To confirm that the patient has paid their hospital utility bills
options.D: To make sure the patient's internet connection speed is fast enough

explanation: Identity verification protects patient privacy and ensures sensitive medical details are not disclosed to the wrong party. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why do nurses monitor blood tests like prealbumin during high calorie therapy?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of urine produced daily
options.B: To determine the patient's current level of physical pain
options.C: To check how well the body is processing and storing nutrients
options.D: To screen for underlying genetic disorders

explanation: Blood proteins like prealbumin change quickly when nutritional status improves, helping us see if our nutrition plan is hitting the mark. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h5)

question: In the famous Swiss Cheese Model of safety, what do the holes in the cheese represent?

options.A: Missing pages in a patient chart
options.B: Weaknesses or flaws in safety defenses
options.C: The specific names of careless workers
options.D: Physical gaps in hospital room walls

explanation: Great job! Each hole stands for a specific system weakness that could potentially let an error slip past. You're building solid clinical reasoning! [learn more](GST319_U5_T6#GST319_U5_T6_h2)

question: What usually causes bleeding inside the skull during severe fetal moulding?

options.A: High blood pressure caused by maternal pushing
options.B: Lack of vitamin K in the newborn circulation
options.C: Stretching and tearing of bridging veins inside the skull
options.D: Rupture of scalp arteries from vacuum suction

explanation: Spot on. When the skull bones overlap too severely, they stretch and strain the tiny veins inside, causing them to tear and bleed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h4)

question: Why does cigarette smoking greatly increase a person's risk of getting a lower respiratory infection?

options.A: It puts extra oxygen in the blood, which attracts germs.
options.B: It seals the air sacs shut so no air enters.
options.C: It paralyzes and destroys the tiny hairs (cilia) that sweep dirt out of the airways.
options.D: It stops the stomach from making acid.

explanation: Smoke damages the cilia—the microscopic brooms of the respiratory tract. Without them working, mucus and germs get trapped in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h9)

question: What is a common misconception about herbal and complementary medications?

options.A: They can only be bought with a doctor's prescription
options.B: They are chemically identical to synthetic antibiotics
options.C: They never interact with standard hospital drugs
options.D: They are completely harmless because they are natural

explanation: Patients often think natural means safe, but herbs contain active chemicals that can cause serious side effects or drug interactions. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why does a unit manager need to understand both patient advocacy and hospital rules?

options.A: To avoid ever having to care for patients directly
options.B: To replace the hospital director when they are away
options.C: To enforce rules while still protecting patient and staff welfare
options.D: To ensure the hospital makes a profit on every bed

explanation: Spot on! The manager acts like a bridge—they make sure hospital guidelines are followed, but they also stand up to protect the safety and rights of both patients and staff. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h1)

question: You notice a care assistant rushing an elderly resident through a meal. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Educate the assistant on patient-centered feeding techniques and safety
options.B: Report the assistant to the police for physical abuse immediately
options.C: Ignore the incident since assistants are trained separately
options.D: Take over feeding all residents in the facility personally

explanation: Well done! As a nurse, you supervise support staff. Teaching them the right, gentle way to feed residents ensures safe and dignified care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T1#GNS324_U5_T1_h2)

question: During a home visit, your patient lets their adult child answer all your medical questions. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Refuse to discuss the care plan until the child leaves the room
options.B: Insist that the client make decisions completely on their own
options.C: Include the child in health education and care planning discussions
options.D: Report the family dynamic as a case of undue financial influence

explanation: Great choice! Respecting family structures means working together with the person they trust to speak for or help them. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h3)

question: In research data, what is a 'wild code'?

options.A: A missing signature on a patient consent form
options.B: An emergency code called when a patient's heart stops
options.C: A secret password used to access the hospital computer network
options.D: A number that falls outside the allowed range of valid responses

explanation: A wild code is just an accidental typo—like typing '8' when a question only has options 1, 2, or 3! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h3)

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triad used to study how diseases spread?

options.A: Infection, disease, and recovery
options.B: Pathogen, vector, and symptom
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Human, animal, and bacteria

explanation: Think of the triad as a stool with three legs: the infectious agent, the susceptible host, and the environment. All three must interact for an infection to take root! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h1)

question: A client wants a refill for her birth control, but admits she might already be pregnant. What should you do first?

options.A: Perform a pregnancy test before giving the refill
options.B: Tell her to double her dose for the next week
options.C: Switch her to a progestin-only pill right away
options.D: Refill the prescription immediately without questions

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out an existing pregnancy before continuing hormonal contraceptives to protect both the client and potential pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h4)

question: Why must nurses alter health assessments across different life stages?

options.A: Hospital policies require a different form for every single year of life
options.B: Medical equipment only works properly on elderly patients
options.C: Adults do not need physical examinations like children do
options.D: Different age groups face distinct health risks and developmental needs

explanation: A newborn needs different checks than a teenager or an older adult because their bodies and life risks change over time. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h3)

question: In many homes, unfair food sharing puts which group at the highest risk of poor nutrition?

options.A: Young children and pregnant or lactating women.
options.B: Older teenage boys who play sports.
options.C: Elderly grandparents who live independently.
options.D: Adult male wage earners who work outside the home.

explanation: You're right! Even though their bodies need extra nutrients for growth and health, these groups often end up with the smallest shares. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h5)

question: Why do established rectovaginal fistulas rarely heal on their own?

options.A: The tract becomes lined with epithelium
options.B: Bowel movements constantly stretch the perineum
options.C: Vaginal acidity dissolves new tissue growth
options.D: Continuous high blood pressure prevents clotting

explanation: Once epithelial tissue lines the abnormal passage, the body treats the tract as a normal surface, preventing natural closure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary cause of occupational lung diseases?

options.A: Smoking cigarettes without using a proper filter
options.B: Breathing in harmful workplace dusts and chemicals
options.C: Severe bacterial infections caught in the community
options.D: Inherited genetic defects of the respiratory tract

explanation: These conditions are directly caused by inhaling hazardous substances present in the work environment over a long period. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)
